 Set as preferred source Listen Summarise Japan coach Hajime Moriyasu will leave next week, after the Asian Cup was postponed to December 2027 because of “exceptional circumstances” and Houthi attacks in the host country.
 Moriyasu’s last games will be friendlies against Brazil and Paraguay in Singapore on Nov 14 and Nov 17, ending his spell as Japan’s longest-serving coach.
 The JFA cancelled a planned Dec 30 warm-up in Osaka. President Tsuneyasu Miyamoto said it was an “important opportunity” but the new schedule forced the decision.
 AI generated
 TOKYO – Japan coach Hajime Moriyasu will step down next week, the country’s football association said on Nov 13 , cutting short his tenure in the wake of the 2027 Asian Cup’s postponement .
 Moriyasu, Japan’s longest-serving coach, was originally set to lead the team at the Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia in January before handing the reins to current Under-23 boss Go Oiwa .
 But the Asian Football Confederation announced last week that the tournament would be pushed back to December 2027 due to “exceptional circumstances” in the region, following Houthi attacks on the host country.
 That left Moriyasu in limbo, with Japan Football Association (JFA) chiefs last week declining to clarify when the coaching handover would take place.
 They said on Nov 13 that Japan’s friendlies in Singapore against Brazil on Nov 14 and Paraguay on Nov 17 would be Moriyasu’s last in charge.
 The 58-year-old took over after the 2018 World Cup.
 He led Japan to shock wins over Germany and Spain on the way to a last-16 defeat on penalties to Croatia at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.
 He took them to the last 32 at the 2026 World Cup in North America, where they lost 2-1 to Brazil after a last-minute goal.
 Moriyasu was set to lead the team in an Asian Cup warm-up friendly against a yet-to-be-named opponent in Osaka on Dec 30.
 The JFA said that the game had been cancelled.
 “We had regarded this game as an important opportunity to strengthen the Japan team and we had been making thorough preparations,” JFA president Tsuneyasu Miyamoto said in a statement.
 “But following the postponement of the Asian Cup and considering the national team’s schedule, we have decided to cancel the game.” AFP
